evidence: 0120: Migration 0120_outreach_health_id_unclaimed.sql (placeholder; releases right after 0119, which it extends) plus its runtime-grants.sql block. WHAT IT DOES: a Health ID can be created at an outreach for a person with no email (and possibly no phone), with every guard of 0119 (campaign membership checked in the command, not redacted, not a sealed demo or QA group, not suspended, 18 or over, one Health ID per registration). The patient (name and sex only: no contact, no date of birth) and its Health ID identifier are created with NO account and no contact-verified assurance, so nobody can sign in until the person claims it (the claim flow comes after the campaign). 0119's identity.outreach_registration_health_ids gains created_via ('email' default, 'unclaimed') and possible_duplicate; account_id and challenge_id become nullable, null exactly for an unclaimed Health ID (check constraints). New owner-only identity.outreach_health_id_claims holds the claim code's keyed HMAC only (180 days, 5 attempts) with the OTP key version it was keyed with (hmac_key_version), and the registration's unproven phone (encrypted, lookup HMAC, key version), kept off the patient so it never blocks the number's real owner. A phone on a real patient is refused; a phone on another live (unexpired, not out of attempts) unclaimed claim is flagged possible_duplicate, never refused; with no phone, an active patient with the same name and sex is flagged, never refused. The claim's phone is removed when the registration is redacted (trigger) and once the claim can no longer be used (expired, out of attempts or invalidated; identity.outreach_health_id_scrub_claims, run by each creation and by 0116's retention sweep, whose body 0119 left is changed in place, md5-pinned before and checked after). identity.outreach_health_id_counts gives counts only for the platform admin; identity.outreach_registration_health_ids_for is replaced to also answer created_via. Audit rows carry ids and the phoneOnRecord flag only (never the duplicate flag, which facility audit readers would see). Existing records stay 'email' (post-check). || 0121: Migration 0121_outreach_registration_read_once.sql (placeholder; releases right after 0120) plus its runtime-grants.sql lines. WHAT IT DOES: the two read policies on outreach.registration_cases (outreach_registration_cases_read, permissive; outreach_registration_campaign_read, restrictive) and identity.outreach_registration_health_ids_for(uuid[]) keep exactly their rules but evaluate the session-constant parts once per query instead of once per row: the session facility and outreach.context_allows(session facility, 'outreach.registration.read'); campaign membership through the new outreach.session_campaign_pairs() (the session membership's (campaign, facility) pairs, read as outreach.registration_campaign_member reads them: SECURITY DEFINER, STABLE, the same owner, search_path and EXECUTE grantees, copied from that function); and outreach.privileged_run_active('retention'). outreach-api's registration list stops repeating outreach.registration_campaign_member in its WHERE (the restrictive policy applies it; no runtime role can start a retention run, so outreach-api never reads inside one). Nothing else changes: the create, update, retention and resolve policies, the other functions and every grant but the new helper's. WHO SEES WHICH ROW: unchanged. On a database with 200,000 patients and 511 registrations, every session (organiser, volunteers, a volunteer removed from the campaign, a member whose membership is deactivated, another group's volunteer, a suspended group's organiser, a hospital nurse, wrong purpose, wrong facility, no session, retention runs) times every hid_* role, 10,440 results (rows visible, the list, the duplicate hint, the Health ID lookup, health checks visible, an update of each fixture row, Identity's registration read) were identical before and after 0121 (same sha256); the suite outreach-registration-read-once.integration.sql (96 comparisons with the pre-0121 expressions, 22 named cases) passes before and after. SPEED (outreach-day load test, 500 people, 5 volunteers, 200,000 patients, day at 30x speed): registration median 141 ms -> 55 ms, p95 612 -> 248, max 1,508 -> 420; at 500 registrations the list 1.9 s -> 11 ms, the duplicate hint 1.2 s -> 5 ms, the Health ID lookup for 100 registrations 434 ms -> 8 ms; no lock wait over 10 ms. LOCKS: ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on outreach.registration_cases for ALTER POLICY, NOWAIT, at most 5 seconds (55P03). OLD SERVICES: today's outreach-api (with the repeated filter) reads exactly the same rows. ROLLBACK: a migration restoring the two policy expressions and 0120's function body; outreach.session_campaign_pairs() may stay.
